correctness.rationale: The donor/recipient strict upper transfers are bijective to the edges of B_lambda. Two distinct upper neighbors are adjacent precisely when their donors or recipients agree. This is the line graph of a connected bipartite graph: its star simplices form a good cover whose nerve is B_lambda. Since same-height partitions are nonadjacent, simultaneous attachments are cones on connected graph-like links. The old stage is simply connected by induction from the one-point top-height stage; every map from a connected graph to it is null. Cofiber splitting gives wedges of S2, while the integral pair LES gives canonical injections and H1(B_lambda) quotients. The cycle rank is sum_b(k_b-1)=w(lambda), and marking M,a,b gives the positive partition generating series. Independent direct transfer/neighbor check over 194 partitions for n<=11 verified the strict upper-link line graph and cycle rank; no finite check is presented as proof of the all-n statement.

value.rationale: This identifies precisely when primitive integral homology classes are born and proves their survival under a canonical height filtration. These persistence/associated-graded data are not specified by the known global wedge type or alternating face-vector sum, and provide a motivated partition-theoretic homology interpretation.

final_claim: For every n>=1 the descending height sublevel filtration of the partition-transfer clique complex has nullhomotopic connected upper-link cone attachments. At a partition lambda, the integral two-sphere birth rank is w(lambda)=#{(b,a) in S(lambda)^2:b+2<=a<max S(lambda)}. The canonically identified associated-graded integral H2 is the sum of upper bipartite-graph cycle lattices.
